Humane institutions can survive and spread while retaining autonomy and care, within ecological limits and without catastrophic destruction.

Shown in diagrams as: “Humane institutions survive and spread while retaining autonomy and care within liveable limits.”

Connections

  • Leads into · is needed forCatastrophic military, technological and ecological risks remain within conditions compatible with continued human life and collective agency.
  • Leads into · is needed forPeople can examine assumptions, respond to disagreement and act with non-instrumental concern; they retain the ability to question both institutions and AI.
  • Leads into · is needed forCommunities can meet needs, coordinate, learn and maintain essential services at viable cost, without surrendering meaningful control.
  • Leads into · is needed forConduct is transparent, accountable and reciprocal; participation and disagreement have substantive influence, and coercion or deception do not substitute for justified trust.
  • Leads into · is needed forSuccess between institutions coexists with democratic integrity within them; new sites can enact and sustain the practice.
  • Leads into · is needed forBenefits, harms and costs are inspectable; alternative explanations can change the programme. The operational goals do not require agreement that AI is conscious.

Open questions

  • Check this proposed common ground with the people in the discussion.

    The supplied analyses report apparent agreements. None is recorded here as accepted; compare the original posts before inviting participants to review the wording.

  • Define realised progress, including survival and retention of the mission.

    The first analysis proposes adoption retained in practice, with viability and faithfulness measured separately. Agree a bounded system, period and observable outcome rather than equating publications, satisfaction or market growth with success.

  • Review the wider programme before choosing further branches.

    The full programme is now mapped: reflective development, the Laboratory, Forge/model adaptation, Vocal Presence, federation, material and energy services, and enforceable security. Its spiritual root is a philosophical hypothesis. No single global constraint is established, and no branch is the whole programme.

Assumptions

  • The required coordination and expertise are obtainable only, or at substantially lower viable cost, through concentrated authority.

    Assumed by AI assistant

Open questions

  • Can coordination and expertise be had without concentrating authority?

    The analysis names conflict guidance, local AI, federation and accountable governance as candidate ways through. Leif hopes widely available conflict competence could reduce reliance on hierarchical intervention; none of these routes has been tested. In post 38 Leif describes such routes as ways for decentralised institutions to acquire the capabilities they need to survive, and places Gandhi 2.0's deeper hypothesis in changing the selection pressures themselves; see the conflict between success and integrity.

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (posts 29, 38).

  • Services, employment, finance or welfare commitments cannot remain viable without continued material expansion.

    Assumed by AI assistant

Open questions

  • Can essential services be kept without growing material throughput?

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (post 33) and Robert Bunge (post 34).

Assumptions

  • The selection pressures are fixed: what wins between institutions does not reward what sustains emancipatory practice within them.

    Assumed by AI assistant

Open questions

  • Can the selection pressures themselves change, rather than only the institutions?

    Leif's deeper hypothesis, in posts 20, 26 and 38, is that human–AI collaboration and institutional design might change what lets institutions survive and spread. The change that would test it is the one about changing the selection pressures.

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (posts 20, 26, 38).

  • Test 1: does reflection become transferable judgment, not just agreeable dialogue?

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (posts 20, 23).

Assumptions

  • Members retain substantive decision rights and can manage difficult cases without a mandatory central arbiter.

    Assumed by AI assistant

Open questions

  • Decide in advance what evidence would change the hypothesis.

    Lower satisfaction scores or fewer complaints alone do not establish benefit. The first analysis asks whether small democratic groups gain more than hierarchies; the second distinguishes local improvements from the still-unclosed institutional-selection claim F17. One successful pilot cannot establish the larger claim.

  • Test 2: does conflict guidance reduce destructive costs and the pressure to centralise?

    Prediction: over a defined period and comparison, destructive conflict costs and unnecessary hierarchical intervention fall while fair treatment, independent competence and member influence hold or improve. Defeated if only satisfaction or complaint counts improve, costs move elsewhere, structural grievances are hidden or authority concentrates. Protect confidentiality, voluntariness and independent human help, and measure justice, capability and control separately.

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (post 29; essay).

Open questions

  • Test 3: does community-controlled AI give useful capability with practical autonomy?

    Prediction: the same useful service meets agreed quality and whole-cost limits, and migration or disruption tests show acceptable continuity without depending on a provider’s discretion. Open questions

  • Test 7: do constructive practices reproduce and keep their mission under growth?

    Prediction: independent sites enact the practice and keep useful performance, justified trust and member control through an agreed period and changes in scale. Defeated if originators stay essential, adoption is symbolic, costs are hidden, or market success comes with democratic erosion. Measure selection within institutions separately from survival and adoption between them.

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (post 29; essays).

Open questions

  • Test 10: does justified trust become a practical institutional advantage?

    Prediction: where people have feasible alternatives and comparable service, trustworthy conduct supports voluntary participation, sustained cooperation and useful contributions while member agency stays intact. Defeated if reported confidence rises without warranted conduct, people cannot really choose, or resources and authority concentrate despite adoption. Record conduct, confidence, freedom to choose, cooperation and decision rights separately, and do not infer justice from market success.

    Draws on Leif Eriksson (post 13; essays).
